findings.rationale: Current candidate bytes retain runnable completion clients that accept only caller-supplied CLI acknowledgements and issue /v1/chat/completions requests without loading the fixed authorization aggregate, reconciling the R0-R2 ledger, acquiring the candidate-global capability, or consuming a preallocated slot. The guarded bootstrap executor is therefore not an exclusive model-call boundary, so model execution is not fail-closed even though release remains hard-disabled.
findings.required_action: Route every completion-capable entry point through one non-bypassable candidate-bound authorization boundary. Remove or quarantine direct clients, require either the fixed 24-slot bootstrap authorization or accepted R3 authority before every provider request, and add source-closure and adversarial tests proving no other completion transport is reachable.
findings.title: Runnable completion clients bypass artifact-derived authorization and the 24-slot executor

findings.rationale: The successor contract creates a reachable, exactly 24-slot bootstrap path, but the retained direct completion clients allow other model runs without R3 acceptance. The parent requirement that every non-bootstrap model run require R3 is therefore not satisfied.
findings.required_action: Enforce R3 acceptance at every non-bootstrap completion site and make the fixed bootstrap executor the only pre-R3 provider path.
findings.title: Non-bootstrap model calls remain reachable without R3 acceptance

findings.rationale: The closure report lists hashes and sizes for 192 files from a workspace-external upstream BFCL checkout, while the bundle retains only the tracked-name capture and empty dirty-status capture. The listed BFCL file bytes or a content-addressed source archive are not materialized, so their hashes, imported implementation, Git identity, and tracked-tree replay cannot be independently reconstructed from this bundle.
findings.required_action: Materialize all 192 tracked BFCL bytes or an equivalent content-addressed source archive in the closed bundle, independently verify every path, size, hash, tree identity, and clean-state claim from those bytes, then regenerate the worker closure, identities, source inventory, captures, and review manifest.
findings.title: Upstream BFCL tracked bytes are absent from the closed replay bundle

findings.rationale: The active R1 contract-validation report was generated with scope contracts and contains neither source_inventory nor source_inventory_sha256. Its enclosing stage-author binding carries the current source root, but stage-ledger reconciliation does not make that external root an internal identity of the subordinate validation receipt. The required regeneration from the complete active inventory did not occur.
findings.required_action: Regenerate R1 contract validation with the complete active 404-entry source inventory and require ledger reconciliation to compare the subordinate receipt's internal candidate and source identity before appending successor R1 states and a checkpoint.
findings.title: The R1 contract-validation receipt still lacks the active source inventory
